title: +10 % laser power step
description: pi_lock_c at 25 °C; at 10 ms every laser line steps +10 % in power (0.414 dB), the rings heat themselves more and the lock moves its set point.
frame_reducer_note: each frame is the window (t_s - frame_s, t_s]: means over it unless the unit list says 'last' (value at t_s) or 'min'/'max' (envelope over the window)

lock_reference.note: each ring's own steady operating point (median detuning over the last 5 ms of a 20 ms static pre-run, experiment.self_reference)

drives.note: aggressor_w: power into each aggressor site (window mean); laser_power_factor: chip power of each line relative to nominal (scenario power step x line enable); the cold start's 3 ms laser turn-on ramp is a plant reset protocol, visible in p_in_mw, not in this factor; t_base_k: the die base temperature the thermal model adds every rise to

events.label: metrics start (the lock's start-up peak map ends before this)

signals.name: thermal.t_base_k
signals.doc: Absolute base temperature of the die below the ROM (TEC set point, soak profile, ambient).
signals.path: Disturbance path 1: package / TEC base temperature (s to h)

signals.name: thermal.xpu_rise_k
signals.doc: Temperature rise at the PIC caused by a processor power-state change (not the TEC, not the on-die aggressor).
signals.path: Disturbance path 3: XPU / ASIC power events (10-120 degC/s within ~30 ms at the PIC)

signals.name: thermal.aggressor_w
signals.doc: Power of each on-die aggressor heater, W, >= 0 (a heater can only heat: PAT-1 [0050]).
signals.path: Disturbance path 2: on-die aggressor heater power into the ROM aggressor column (given as power)

signals.name: laser.dfreq_hz
signals.doc: Dynamic line frequency offset in Hz (positive = shorter wavelength). A heating-equivalent sweep is positive: the line moves blue as the resonance would move red.
signals.path: Disturbance path 4: laser wavelength, optical only (sweep emulation, drift, failover)

signals.name: laser.power_delta_db
signals.doc: Change of each line's power at the laser output, dB.
signals.path: Laser: power drift and failover power step (textbook A17)

signals.name: laser.line_enable
signals.doc: Line enable as a power factor in [0, 1].
signals.path: Laser: line enable laser_line_enable (T, B, L)

signals.name: optical.input_loss_delta_db
signals.doc: Change of the laser-to-chip loss, dB (positive = more loss).

signals.name: data.ones_density
signals.doc: Fraction of ones in the transmitted bits.
signals.path: Data path: ones density of the transmitted data

signals.name: data.swing_scale
signals.doc: Factor on the driver swing; 0 is squelch (modulation off, average kept).
signals.path: Data-activity heat: swing_vpp (T, B, N) as a factor on driver.swing_vpp (squelch = 0)

signals.name: tx.bias_offset_v
signals.path: Bias channel: additive bias offset (ripple, droop), always allowed

signals.name: tx.bias_v
signals.doc: Absolute reverse bias set by the scenario.
signals.path: Bias channel: absolute bias when tx.bias is bound to the scenario (scenario A7 relOMA plane)

signals.name: fault.adc_saturate
signals.path: Fault mask: ADC code at full scale (adc_saturate)

signals.name: fault.dac_glitch_codes
signals.path: Fault: heater DAC glitch (proposal: additive heater code after the DAC FIFO, per tick)

inputs.note: every input signal of the compiled scenario (mrm.scenarios.generators.SIGNALS) evaluated every 10 us with the scenario's own evaluator and reduced over each frame (mean, min, max); a signal that does not change in the run is given once ('constant'). 'active': the scenario drives it (it has components); otherwise it holds its default or the config's value

controller_timing.note: ticks of dt_s. Controller steps at phase + j x period; ADC samples of ring n end at phase[n] + j x adc_period after a window of adc_window ticks and are released adc_latency ticks later; a heater command reaches the DAC output dac_latency ticks after it is latched

saturation_counts.note: number of controller steps whose heater command was outside [code_min, code_max] and was clipped, whole run (start-up included)

summary.note: metrics are the engine's own accumulators (every 1 us tick after score_from_s), as `mrm run` reports them

plain_description: The controller pi_lock_c holds all 8 rings at 25 °C. At 10 ms every laser line steps up by 10 % in power (0.414 dB), as a laser failover or drift would. More light heats each ring more (self-heating) and changes what the monitor PD sees. The lock settles at a new point: the lock error is measured about the point the lock held before the step, so the rings end outside the ±5 pm band (largest error 20 pm, ring 6).
